packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-06 — unverified image-only reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. Only the brief, PROMPT.md and the packet images were opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001.jpg, reduced overview)

- image-001.jpg is a reduced overview: one face of a single fragment photographed on black with a colour checker (lower left) and cm scale (right edge). Landscape orientation as photographed, roughly 20 x 12.5 cm (scale reads approx. 13-25 cm vertically).
- Support is light, cockled, with all four corners cut off diagonally (octagonal outline), consistent with reuse as a binding piece. Brown water/paste stains across the middle; a row of wormholes/losses along a horizontal line near the bottom (approx. scale 12) and vertical lines of holes running down the left text block and near the centre.
- Writing: a cursive, fairly rapid hand in brown ink, in two text blocks side by side (left block and right block), separated by a narrow gutter around the centre. Observation only: whether these are two columns of one page or two pages of an opened bifolium I cannot tell from the overview; there is a vertical fold/crease line near the centre.
- Left block: about 6 lines of running prose at top, then a heading in larger letters "Quaestio 2da" (centred-left) followed by a subheading line beginning "De figura ..." (tentatively "De figura et motu stellarum"), then a paragraph beginning "Conclusio ..." Text continues to the bottom edge.
- Right block: about 8-9 lines of prose at top, then lines beginning "Conclusio" further down (two instances visible, roughly at scale 18-19 and at scale 13).
- Superimposed across the middle band is a mirror-image (reversed) offset/ghost of a large black Gothic book script (textura) in several lines; this is offset from another document, not text of this face. I keep it separate and do not transcribe it.
- Lower right corner: modern pencil label, apparently "Stams, StA, Frag. 29r" (reading uncertain; the last element may be "29r" or "29v").
- No running title, coloured rubrics, or marginal glosses distinguishable at overview scale. Heading "Quaestio 2da" is written larger, apparently in the same ink.
- Tentative interpretation (not an identification): a scholastic-style question text (Quaestio / Conclusio structure) on a natural-philosophy topic (stars).

TRANSCRIPTION

002.10  Conclusio 1ma?: figura stellarum est rotunda[...]   ("1ma"/"prima" reading uncertain; possibly a different word, e.g. a short abbreviated form)
002.11  q(uod)? stellae sint eiusdem figurae et nec? cum se[...]

LIMITATIONS AND COVERAGE
- Face 1 (image-001 overview, tiles 002-007): coverage as below. (Note added after this section was first written: image-008 turned out to be the overview of the second face; see FACE 2 below.)
- Read: the top 7 lines and heading/first Conclusio of the left block; the top 13 lines of the right block (fairly connected); the lower right block (connected at line ends); the lower left block only in fragments.
- Largely unread: the centres of the lower-left-block lines (005.04-005.13) and of right-block lines R13-R21, where the reversed black textura offset overlies the brown cursive. A raking-light or colour-channel separation (e.g. a red/brown channel to suppress the black offset) would help there.
- Line assignment between the left halves (005, 006.R) and right halves (006.L, 007) of the same physical line rests on vertical position; the hand slopes, so a one-line misalignment is possible in the lower left block.
- The hand is a cursive with heavy flourishes; frequent abbreviations: q(uod)/q(uia) as "q" with stroke, n(on) as "n" with bar, e(st)/e(sse) as "e" with bar or "ēē", s(ed) as "s" with 3-like sign, p(ar)tes with barred p. Expansions are proposals.
- Nothing beyond the brief's rules was done; no crops made.

==========================================================
FACE 2

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-008.jpg, reduced overview)
- Other face of the same fragment (same octagonal cut outline, mirrored), held flat by two clear plastic weights (upper left-centre and lower right). Pencil label at bottom centre-left, apparently "Stams, StA, Frag. 29v" (last letter uncertain).
- Same cursive hand(s) in brown ink, again two text blocks side by side separated by a vertical fold near the centre. No reversed textura offset on this face; stains and wormhole rows along the top and bottom and down the fold lines.
- Left block: about 8 lines at top, a paragraph break, then a paragraph beginning "Quod ad nonnullos? ..." with a marginal note in the far left margin (2-3 short words, beside lines ~ scale 19-20) and another marginal word at about scale 16 ("etc."?). Lower down a paragraph beginning "Conclusio ..." (approx. scale 15).
- Right block: about 9 lines at top, a paragraph beginning "Dices? ..." (approx. scale 21), and a later paragraph beginning "Ubi? ..." (approx. scale 13). Some lines near the bottom-right are hidden under the lower weight.
- No enlarged heading like "Quaestio" visible on this face at overview scale.

FACE 2 TRANSCRIPTION
